note: Worked at a hometown car wash with three machines: gold tokens for the wash, silver tokens for the vacuum, real quarters for tire shine. Became his go-to analogy for needing different gas tokens per chain.
Keeps a little bitcoin on a hardware wallet in his 'metaphorical sock drawer', and has a fat-finger send story he refuses to finish.
Admitted Jules's 'one slot that takes whatever's in your pocket' analogy works; Jules demanded she 'write it down, date it.'

Spent a summer at a bait shop run by Dale, who posted a sign bragging about throwing out a hundred dead minnows the same week five hundred new ones arrived. 'Getting Dale'd' is now Jules's phrase for falling for burn-style marketing.

Her one-number rule for any deflation claim: 'burned minus emitted.' She also admitted a second Jules analogy works (Dale handing minnows to his regulars as buy-and-distribute), and Jules again made her 'date it.'

At fifteen ran 'the corn route': bought sweet corn at a farm stand for a dollar a dozen, sold it at the lake for three, but his uncle's gas-guzzling truck (charged both ways) and corn wilting in the sun left him with about four dollars for the summer. Now his go-to picture of fees, gas and slippage.
His braai rule for margin of safety: you don't throw the steak on the second the fire's lit, you wait for proper coals, because something always goes wrong.
Admitted a third Jules analogy works (the uncle's truck making five trips = splitting trades multiplies fixed costs); Jules says it's 'already dated, in pen.'
